senses.sense_definition: An absurd pretense or deceptive situation intended to create a pleasant appearance.

examples.text: Everyone knew their marriage was over, but they kept up the <w>charade</w> for the public.
The entire trial was an elaborate <w>charade</w> designed to hide the administration's mistakes.

senses.sense_definition: A single round or performance in a game of charades, where a word or phrase is acted out silently.

examples.text: Her humorous <w>charade</w> had the whole family laughing as they tried to guess the movie title.
During each <w>charade</w>, players are strictly forbidden from speaking or mouthing words.

senses.sense_definition: A type of wordplay or cryptic crossword clue in which several smaller words are joined to form a whole word.

examples.text: This crossword clue is a classic <w>charade</w> combining two short nouns to make a longer answer.
He struggled to solve the complex <w>charade</w> hidden within the daily newspaper puzzle.

senses.sense_definition: A traditional riddle in verse or prose where clues describe each syllable of a word separately, followed by a clue for the whole word.

examples.text: In the nineteenth century, composing a rhyming <w>charade</w> was a popular parlor pastime.
The poet published an enigmatic <w>charade</w> whose final answer puzzled readers for months.

traits.comment: Refers to the historical literary riddle form.

senses.sense_definition: A theatrical performance that resembles the game charades, especially due to exaggerated or amateurish acting.

examples.text: The local theatre production was criticized as a clumsy <w>charade</w> rather than a serious drama.
Critics dismissed the amateur play as little more than an uninspired <w>charade</w>.

senses.sense_definition: To act out something pantomimically, or to pretend or disguise oneself dishonestly.

examples.text: Instead of speaking, she <w>charaded</w> her refusal by shaking her head and waving her arms.
The corrupt official tried to <w>charade</w> as an honest reformer during the press conference.
